relationships.subject: BmK AGAP
relationships.evidence_quote: AGAP, for example, inhibits TRPV1 and KCNQ2/3 currents and spinal MAPK pathways and can extend the duration of lidocaine analgesia, reducing the required local-anesthetic dose in neuropathic models [19,60].

relationships.subject: BmK I
relationships.evidence_quote: At the same time, some scorpion toxins such as BmK I are pronociceptive, enhancing NaV1.8 currents and driving spontaneous pain and mechanical allodynia in rodent models [50].

relationships.subject: BmK AGAP
relationships.evidence_quote: Pairings like AGAP with lidocaine decrease the effective dose by half.

key_findings: Scorpion venom peptides such as BmK AGAP block NaV1.7/NaV1.8 and inhibit TRPV1, giving morphine-comparable analgesia in rodent models.
No purified scorpion peptide has entered randomized trials; venom variability, immunogenicity and off-target effects remain obstacles.
